problem:
Given that ${y}_{0}(x)={e}^{x}$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=4{y}^{2}-8{e}^{x}y+4{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x}
$$

 

find the general solution of the equation.

feedback.problem:
The function ${y}_{0}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,y+({cos}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x).
$$

Express this equation in the Bernoulli form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x){z}^{n}
$$

and state the functions $P(x)$ and $Q(x),$ and the value of $n.$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$,\,Q(x)=$
{{field-2}}
$,\,n=$
{{field-3}}
feedback.worked_solution:
A Riccati differential equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x).
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x$, we have

$$
y=z+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x=(z+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,(z+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+({cos}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x).
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =({z}^{2}+2z\operatorname{cos}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,z-2{cos}^{2}⁡x+({cos}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ {z}^{′}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ={z}^{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {z}^{′} & ={z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is a Bernoulli equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x){z}^{n}
$$

where

$$
P(x)=0,\,Q(x)=1,\,n=2.
$$
